proposals.before: At several sui he lost his father and was raised by his uncle, Director of the Bureau of Armaments Qian; later he followed his mother to the household of Wei Renpu; the emperor's son-in-law Xianxin was his maternal half-brother.
proposals.after: At several sui he lost his father and was raised by his uncle, Vice Director of the Bureau of Operations Qian; later he followed his mother to the household of Wei Renpu; the emperor's son-in-law Xianxin was his maternal half-brother.
proposals.reason: 職方員外郎 is vice director of the Bureau of Operations, not director of a Bureau of Armaments.

proposals.before: Coastal merchants then sailed to trade in foreign goods, while Java, Srivijaya, Parhae, Champa, and other lands also sent annual missions to court, so that rhinoceros horn, ivory, aromatics, medicinals, and other rarities overflowed the storehouses.

proposals.before: His son Minzhong was first made an Attendant Official; while Xun served at the Palace Directorate, Minzhong petitioned that he had studied letters and wished to change rank, and was at once transferred to assistant director in the Court of Judicial Review, rising in time to department director in the Ministry of Revenue.

proposals.before: Son Minzhong was first appointed Attendant Official; while Xun was at the Palace Directorate, he memorialized that he had once studied literature and wished to change rank; he was immediately exchanged to Assistant Director of the Court of Judicial Review, accumulating to Department Head in the Ministry of Public Works.
proposals.after: Son Minzhong was first appointed Attendant Official; while Xun was at the Palace Directorate, Xun memorialized that Minzhong had studied literature and wished to change rank; Minzhong was immediately transferred to Assistant Director of the Court of Judicial Review, later reaching Department Director of the Bureau of Review (Ministry of Revenue).
proposals.reason: 比部郎中 is the Bureau of Review under Revenue, not the Ministry of Public Works; pronouns also collapse father and son.

proposals.before: His original name was Rong; Taizong changed the written form of his name to one signifying smelting ore and said, "It is through firing clay in a kiln that vessels are formed."
proposals.after: His original name was Rong (written 容); Taizong changed it to Rong (鎔) and said, "It is by molding and smelting that vessels are formed."
proposals.reason: The Chinese 陶鎔所以成器也 is a molding/smelting metaphor matching the metal-radical rename 鎔; the English mixes kiln-firing clay with smelting ore.

proposals.before: He was the son of Right Royal Guard Senior General Zhou Jing.
proposals.after: He was the son of Right Leading Army Guard Senior General Jing.
proposals.reason: 右領軍衛 is the Leading Army Guard, not a Royal Guard; the office name is mistranslated.

proposals.before: Tianxiong Military Commissioner Sun Yongyou and Transport Commissioner Yang Chen praised him; he was also sent to inspect border affairs in Sui and Yin prefectures, and on his return his memorial pleased the emperor and he was promoted to Deputy Commissioner of the Saddle and Bridle Repository.

proposals.after: The emperor judged Ying mediocre, timid, and dull, replaced him with Cao Wei, and transferred him to govern Chan Prefecture.

proposals.after: The emperor said Ying was mediocre, cowardly and unwise; Cao Wei replaced him; he was transferred to know Chan Prefecture.

proposals.reason: 澶州 is Chan Prefecture, not Cao Prefecture.

proposals.before: The transport commissioner memorialized his laxness; he was transferred to know Cao Prefecture; within the territory bandits repeatedly appeared; the grand councilors, because Ying held a general's post, could not calm by prestige, and requested moving him to another prefecture.
proposals.after: The transport commissioner memorialized his laxness; he was transferred to know Chan Prefecture; within the territory bandits repeatedly appeared; the grand councilors, because Ying held a general's post, could not calm by prestige, and requested moving him to another prefecture.
proposals.reason: 澶州 is Chan Prefecture, not Cao Prefecture.

proposals.after: Because Chanyuan lay on the Khitan line of attack and its generous grain stipends were hard to give up, he was again appointed to govern Chan Prefecture.

proposals.after: Also because Chanyuan faced the Khitan thrust, relying on its generous grain stipends, he was again ordered to know Chan Prefecture.

proposals.after: When the emperor went to Chan Prefecture and the Khitan sought peace, Jiying took part in the strategic consultations.

proposals.after: Following the emperor to Chan Prefecture, when the Khitan requested peace and strategy was consulted, Jiying participated.

proposals.before: While Xia and Yibu were troubled by raids, Xian memorialized, "In recent years the frontier has not been quiet: Li Jiqian has turned ungrateful in Ling and Xia, Wang Xiaobo has rebelled in Ba and Qiong, and armies have been raised both in Hexi and in the southwest.

proposals.before: At the time the imperial carriage was ascending the mausoleum; Xian told his guests and aides: "My remaining years and rank have reached the extreme; today the Son of Heaven's road passes through Hulao—I cannot once bow to the dust of the attendant carriage; this is a remaining regret!"
